before: Prerequisites: semantic sections and JavaScript DOM selection (javascript-58). A template stores inert markup; its contents do not become ordinary rendered children of the surrounding document. The template’s content property exposes a DocumentFragment containing that markup.

In the supplied JavaScript bridge below, cloneNode(true) makes a deep copy of the fragment including descendants. append(copy) inserts its nodes into the destination and consumes that copied fragment’s children; the original template remains reusable. after: `<template>` stores HTML for later use. Its contents are inert: they are kept aside instead of appearing on the page. JavaScript can later copy them into the visible page.

A normal `<div>` does not store its contents this way. If you replace template with div, the card becomes ordinary page content straight away. Keep template when you want to save the pattern for later.

This example stores one card and leaves a place for future cards. ```html
``` `card-template` names the stored pattern. The article inside it is not shown yet. The empty section `cards` is the destination where a later script can put a copy.

before.question: Replacing template with div has which effect before any JavaScript runs?
choices: The div automatically gains a content fragment.
The article becomes an ordinary document descendant.
before.explanation: A div is an ordinary container, not inert template storage. Its descendants enter the document immediately.

after.question: You replace template with div. What happens before any JavaScript runs?
choices: The div gets special template storage.
The article becomes ordinary page content.
after.explanation: A div is a normal container. A template keeps its contents aside until they are used.
